messages:
incidents-bot: PAGING -> p99 streaming tail latency spike detected in cluster us-west-2 (svc: inference-stream). Alerting oncall. Incident ID: INC-29950. Initial p99 jumped from 420ms -> 1.8s over last 5m. :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): On it. seeing the same in console, p95 ~ 600ms, p99 ~ 1.8s, error rate unchanged. Starting triage now.

kevin: @maria any visible deploys in the last hour? compilepath/rt update?

maria (oncall): Checking deploys... UI shows a canary machine image roll and a runtime kernel bump rolled 35m ago: `runtime:v2026.03.14+trt8patch`.

tara: That build included the new TRT8/flashattn kernel variant + a compile flag `-O3 -mfma` change that landed yesterday in staging and then promoted. I flagged it last night but CI perf looked fine.

jonah: Adding telemetry: GPU stall metric `kv_cache_queue_time` spiked along with decode tail. Logs show frequent `page_miss` entries around same timestamps. Suspect paging interaction with new kernel scheduling.

runtime_amy: Repro locally with a short streaming workload and the new kernel? I can run a quick microbenchmark on a dev box (same cuda driver). Gives us a repro if we can see the tail on decode.

kevin: Please capture `nvidia-smi dmon` and runtime logs. Also dump `dmesg` for any OOM or page fault churn.

maria (oncall): Collected baseline metrics and tail traces. P95/P99 waterfall attached (will paste snippets).

maria (oncall): ```
# sample tail traces (shortened)
2026-03-15T01:02:10.123Z svc=inference-stream req=abc123 step=decode kernel=trt8-flashattn lat_ms=1832 kv_cache_hit=false page_miss=true
2026-03-15T01:02:10.456Z svc=inference-stream req=def456 step=decode kernel=trt8-flashattn lat_ms=1490 kv_cache_hit=false page_miss=true
```

jonah: Those `page_miss=true` events line up with spikes. If the new kernel defers or blocks on certain memcpy patterns we could see cascaded stalls.

tara: Quick check: the compile flag we added changes vectorization hints; on Ampere/Turing it can expose different SPM behavior. Another clue: telemetry shows more thread preemptions during decode.

sre_lead: Customer impact? Any high-tier customers seeing errors/timeouts?

maria (oncall): No 5xxs; just elevated latencies. One enterprise customer (acme-inc) reported slowed streaming responsiveness but no disconnects. I've alerted SE team.

kevin: Mitigation options: 1) Roll back runtime kernel to previous known-good image (safe, immediate), 2) Hotpatch compile flags (risky), 3) Route streaming traffic to lower-latency pool (capacity permitting). Thoughts?

runtime_amy: I can prepare a rollforward patch that reverts the kernel scheduling tweak and keep TRT8/flashattn otherwise. Build takes ~20m. But rollback of the full runtime image is fastest.

maria (oncall): Can we do a targeted rollback for streaming nodes only? We have label `role=streaming` in k8s. Prefer minimal blast radius.

infra_bot: Deployment plan detected: previous image `runtime:v2026.03.13` available in registry. Rolling back `deployment/inference-stream` replica set to revision 42 will take ~3-5min per AZ.

tara: One more ask: capture a flame graph before doing rollback. If we roll back we'll lose the in-flight traces we could use to root cause. Can we dump pprof quickly to S3?

maria (oncall): Doing pprof dump now -> uploading to s3://redwood-dumps/INC-29950/pprof-01.tar.gz. Link: https://s3.redwood/INC-29950/pprof-01.tar.gz :eyes:

kevin: OK proceed with targeted rollback in us-west-2 canary and then monitor p99. Maria, coordinate with infra to roll back one AZ first. I'll stand by to approve full rollback.

maria (oncall): `kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-stream --to-revision=42 --record` -> starting AZ-a now.

infra_bot: AZ-a rollback started. Pod old->new replace 3 pods. Expected 180s.

maria (oncall): AZ-a: p99 dropping to ~550ms within 2min. Re-run traces show fewer `page_miss` flags. AZ-b still elevated.

jonah: Good signal that kernel variant is causal. Can we do a patched build that disables the `kv_cache_prefetch` path introduced in v2026.03.14? If that's quick, maybe safer than full rollback.

runtime_amy: I can produce a patch to flip `KV_CACHE_PREFETCH=0` and run a quick canary in AZ-b. Build and push will be ~25m including smoke tests.

kevin: Given AZ-a improved, let's continue rolling back AZ-b and AZ-c while amy builds the patch. If patch passes, we can redeploy a patched image and avoid losing other runtime fixes.

maria (oncall): Rolling AZ-b now. Monitoring.

infra_bot: AZ-b rollback complete. p99 there falling to ~520ms. Global p99 now ~540ms.

sre_lead: Keep customer comms updated. SE has been notified. No SLA breach yet but we're watching p99 window. Add timeline in incident doc.

maria (oncall): Incident doc updated: https://confluence.redwood/INC-29950 - root cause suspected: kernel scheduling change in runtime:v2026.03.14 interacting badly with paging patterns -> decode tail latency.

tara: After rollback, let's run the reproducer across a matrix of CUDA driver versions and instance types. I want to verify if this is driver sensitive.

jonah: Also file a metrics alert to detect `page_miss` correlation with any future kernel promotions. Maybe a canary gate.

kevin: Amy, when patch image is ready, we'll canary it to AZ-c only and compare tails. If good, we can replace rollbacks with patched rollout.

runtime_amy: Patch pushed to registry as `runtime:v2026.03.14+kfix01`. Canarying AZ-c now with one replica.

maria (oncall): Canary pod report: p99 ~ 560ms, page_miss events minimal. Looks similar to rolled-back baseline.

kevin: Run full AZ-c with patched image gradually (max surge 1). If anything spikes revert back to rolled-back image.

maria (oncall): Rolling AZ-c to patched image now.

infra_bot: AZ-c patch rollout in progress.

maria (oncall): AZ-c patched, global p99 stable ~530ms. No regression after 10m.

sre_lead: Next steps: 1) Keep monitoring for 60m, 2) Postmortem to track why compile flag interacted with paging, 3) Add canary gating to pipeline. Assign owners: runtime_amy for patch PR, tara for compile-flag review, jonah for metrics alerts.

kevin: @runtime_amy open PR referencing INC-29950 and include microbenchmark results. @tara pair with amy on bisect.

maria (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. If anything, page @kevin and follow the escalation policy. For now marking incident as mitigated. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT INC-29950 status -> MITIGATED. Duration 42m. Pager cleared.

maria (oncall): Thanks team. Will add final notes and timeline to the postmortem template.

kevin: Great job. Follow-up items prioritized in backlog.

runtime_amy: I'll attach bench results and flamegraphs to the postmortem.

tara: Also propose adding a test to our premerge perf suite that simulates high prefix paging patterns.

jonah: Filed alert PR to correlate `page_miss` -> p99, linking to this incident.

maria (oncall): Closing thread; incident doc updated. If anything else crops up reopen. :pray:
